destination.name: Innamincka
destination.tagline: Remote Cooper Creek outpost of waterholes, wetlands and Burke and Wills history.
destination.description: Innamincka is a small township on Cooper Creek in South Australia's far north-east, home to about 15 permanent residents. The former Australian Inland Mission building is now the national parks visitor centre, with displays on the Yandruwandha and Yawarrawarrka Traditional Owners, pastoral settlement and the Burke and Wills expedition. Innamincka Regional Reserve covers more than 1.3 million hectares of creek waterholes and arid country. Malkumba-Coongie Lakes National Park, about 100 km north-west, is a Ramsar-listed wetland.
whyVisit: Paddle the waterholes of Cooper Creek
Camp and fish in the outback
Follow the Burke and Wills story

goodToKnow.title: Check road conditions first
goodToKnow.detail: Access is by the Strzelecki Track via Leigh Creek, so read the latest Desert Parks Bulletin before setting out.

goodToKnow.title: Floods close the parks
goodToKnow.detail: Flooding has closed Malkumba-Coongie Lakes and parts of the reserve, so check park alerts before you go.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the most comfortable. Summer is very hot and dry, and good rain brings wildflowers.
